entries.definition: subdued or brought low in condition or status
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Ambiguous by design. It can mean genuinely moved, or beaten and admitting it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sharper, because culture is treated as something the person declined to acquire.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plainest way to say a note or a passport is not forged; no compliment is intended.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Surpassing praise, with a note of polish and craft.
examples: a superb performance from the whole cast

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Light and childlike; affectionate of children, slightly diminishing of adults.
examples: The girls giggled when the rock star came into the classroom

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Curiosity aimed at ideas rather than people, and neutral for it.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The animal metaphor, and easily confused with the unrelated sense meaning attractive.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Of a sum or a gesture - it praises the scale, and implies it exceeded what was owed.

entries.definition: (of a woman or girl) slender and graceful like a sylph
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Poetic praise - slender and light as a spirit.

entries.definition: so extremely ugly as to be terrifying
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Ugliness that actively drives people away.

entries.definition: involving deductive reasoning from a general principle to a necessary effect; not supported by fact
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Formal and academic - at home in philosophy, logic, and law; describes reasoning that comes before experience or evidence.
examples: We cannot assume a priori that the plan will succeed.

entries.definition: satisfied or showing satisfaction with things as they are
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The plainest form, and often used of accepting less than one wanted.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The standard accusation: the speaker is impressed with themselves and has said so.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Political, and it scales from a parent to a state without changing meaning.
examples: the timid child of authoritarian parents

entries.definition: (used of sums of money) so small in amount as to deserve contempt
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: In British use this is the standard word for stingy; American readers hear *cruel* instead.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Points at whoever caused it - the anger is presented as a reasonable response.

entries.definition: affecting extreme elegance in dress and manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Elegance turned into a project, and visibly so.

entries.definition: in a dishonest and fraudulent manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *fraudulent*: the legal word: it implies a crime has been committed, not merely a lie told.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The unhyphenated spelling, commoner now than the hyphen.

entries.definition: subdued or brought low in condition or status
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Status, not disposition; the older sense that *humble origins* still carries.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Empty of sense - condemns the content, not the person.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mocks refinement as performance - the word describes the walk, and means the person.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Unfashionable and entirely sincere; it praises the person, not the sum.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *chintzy*: slides between stingy and shoddy; either way it is a sneer at what was provided.
examples: their rich uncle treated them rather chintzily

entries.definition: (used of sums of money) so small in amount as to deserve contempt
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Said of the sum, not the person - an amount so small it insults whoever receives it.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Raises the subject rather than merely approving of them; close to worship.

entries.definition: worn or shabby from overuse or (of pages) from having corners turned down
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The clipped form, and rare enough to be mistaken for the anatomy word.
examples: a somewhat dog-eared duke … a bit run down
an old book with dog-eared pages

entries.definition: limp and soiled as if dragged in the mud
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pitiable rather than blamed - the rain did this, not the person.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *precious*: affectation as a whole manner - too studied to be trusted.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The sound is the meaning, and it is far too cheerful to condemn much.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and slightly distant, as though reported rather than witnessed.

entries.definition: so extremely ugly as to be terrifying
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Extreme and repellent - among the harshest words available.
examples: a hideous scar left by the fire

entries.definition: perceive with attention; direct one's gaze towards; look
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The neutral verb; everything else in the family adds a judgement to it.
examples: She looked over the expanse of land

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the excess, and implies the eagerness spoiled what it wanted.
examples: overeager in his pursuit of the girl

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Technical and cool; used of marriages and arrangements rather than of feelings.

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The broadest word in the family and the one with the most to lose.

entries.definition: devouring or craving food in great quantities
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Adds hunger to the manner of eating; it watches the food the way a predator would.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Unyielding and unsmiling; it judges the manner as much as the will.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Understated - withholds beauty rather than asserting ugliness.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The absence of feeling, not its violence. A cold refusal need never raise its voice.

entries.definition: having wisdom that comes with age and experience
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Wisdom that came with age, and the noun stands just behind the adjective.

entries.definition: designed to deceive or mislead either deliberately or inadvertently
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Stops short of accusation: it reports the effect, and leaves the intent unstated.
examples: statistics can be presented in ways that are misleading

entries.label: positive
entries.tone: A marketing word before it was a compliment, and it still sounds like packaging.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *arrogant*: condemns self-importance as unearned - the confidence is real, the entitlement is not.
examples: in the old days she had been harsh and stiff; afraid of her husband and yet arrogantly proud that she had a husband strong and fierce enough to make her afraid

entries.definition: lacking and reflecting lack of pity or compassion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The institutional word - it is conditions, treatment and policies that get called inhumane.
examples: humans are innately inhumane; this explains much of the misery and suffering in the world
biological weapons are considered too inhumane to be used

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British and total: the laziness is presented as going all the way through.

entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and rare - the deceiving is deliberate and rather cold.

entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Meets the requirement - the language of reports and inspections, not of praise.
examples: the step makes a satisfactory seat
